title: Super-resolution imaging via photon enumeration

key_results: Super-resolution imaging via photon enumeration (S-RIPE) achieves sub-nanometer localization accuracy for multiple sources; >10× resolution improvement demonstrated for fluorescence microscopy
comments: Passive super-resolution approach leveraging photon-number distributions provides robust, alignment-free alternative to spatial mode decomposition methods, enabling enhancement of existing systems without prior knowledge of sources.

model_io.model: Photon enumeration super-resolution imaging (S-RIPE)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Photon-number distributions enable sub-diffraction-limit spatial resolution without precise alignment
hypotheses.result: Demonstrated >10× resolution improvement with sub-nanometer localization accuracy for multiple sources

title: Supramolecular protein block copolymers encode presynaptic active-zone nanolattices
task: Engineer self-assembling nanomaterials with programmable spatial organization using supramolecular protein block copolymers
key_results: ELKS and RIM form hexagonal lattices with ~60 nm dot diameter and ~130 nm spacing; stoichiometry and client protein incorporation (RIMBP2, Liprin-α3) systematically alter lattice morphology; model validated against reconstituted assemblies and native neuronal synapses
comments: Block-copolymer theory combined with super-resolution nanoscopy reveals minimal scaffold module sufficient for active-zone architecture, establishing general principles for engineering programmable biological nanomaterials.

model_io.model: Supramolecular protein assembly with block-copolymer theory

hypotheses.hypothesis: Orthogonal self-association coupled with specific ELKS-RIM binding generates hexagonal lattices
hypotheses.result: Reconstitution of minimal scaffold module produces regular lattices matching native active-zone organization

hypotheses.hypothesis: Client protein incorporation systematically alters lattice structure
hypotheses.result: RIMBP2 and Liprin-α3 incorporation produces measurable changes in spacing and morphology

title: Enhanced laser-driven ion acceleration through electromagnetic energy coupling in annular sector targets
task: Enhance laser-driven ion acceleration using annular sector target geometry
key_results: Annular sector target increases electromagnetic coupling proxy from 0.156 to 0.616 and electron temperature from 0.94 to 4.46 MeV; proton cutoff energy increases from 9.29 to 16.82 MeV at τ≈400 fs
comments: PIC simulations demonstrate that curved geometry enhances laser-electron coupling and directs particle transport, with hotter electron populations driving improved ion acceleration rather than geometric focusing alone.

model_io.model: 2D Particle-In-Cell (PIC) Target Normal Sheath Acceleration

hypotheses.hypothesis: Annular sector geometry produces stronger electromagnetic energy coupling than flat targets
hypotheses.result: Coupling proxy increases 3.95× (0.156→0.616) with median electron temperature rising 4.75×

hypotheses.hypothesis: Geometric ion convergence provides independent cutoff-energy gain
hypotheses.result: Trajectory diagnostics show improved acceleration driven primarily by enhanced electron heating, not geometric focusing

title: Unifying charge transport and exciton dynamics in Cs2TeCl6: evidence of polaronic conduction governed by electron–phonon coupling
task: Unify charge transport and exciton dynamics in Cs₂TeCl₆ through electron-phonon coupling analysis
key_results: Activation energy ~0.13 eV consistent across electrical and optical measurements; Urbach energy 0.671±0.002 eV; indirect bandgap 2.66±0.05 eV; overlapping large-polaron tunneling (OLPT) governs AC response; photo-induced lattice stiffening confirms strong electron-phonon coupling
comments: Comprehensive multimodal characterization establishes common energetic scale between thermally-activated transport and exciton recombination without requiring single microscopic origin, revealing polaronic conduction in lead-free double perovskite.

model_io.model: Cs₂TeCl₆ lead-free perovskite characterization

hypotheses.hypothesis: Common activation energy emerges from unified framework connecting disorder, electron-phonon coupling, and structural confinement
hypotheses.result: ~0.13 eV activation energy consistently measured in both electrical transport and optical recombination

hypotheses.hypothesis: Overlapping large-polaron tunneling (OLPT) describes dispersive AC response
hypotheses.result: Temperature-dependent frequency exponent agrees with OLPT model; photo-induced lattice stiffening confirms strong electron-phonon coupling

title: Magnetic response of back-biased proximity sensors under projectile motion: detection limits and dead-zone effects
task: Analyze magnetic field sensitivity limits for velocity measurement of moving projectiles
key_results: Nonmagnetic conductors detectable across wide velocity range; ferromagnetic projectiles exhibit detection dead-zone where field perturbation becomes negligible due to competing magnetization and eddy-current effects
comments: Finite element study identifies fundamental limits of back-biased proximity sensing relevant to ballistic velocity measurement in denied environments.

model_io.model: Finite element magnetic field simulation

hypotheses.hypothesis: Geometric features can modify and partially compensate for dead-zone effects
hypotheses.result: Confirmed through parametric investigation of geometry influence
